posts.title: The backlash about data centers might really just be about electricity
posts.summary: This story originally appeared in The Algorithm, our weekly newsletter on AI. To get stories like this in your inbox first, sign up here. As voters went to the polls across the US last week, I was in Ashburn, Virginia, part of what’s known as Data Center Alley—the world’s largest data center hub. It’s also where…
bullets: The growing public backlash against data centers is increasingly driven by physical electricity constraints rather than abstract cultural concerns.
Data centers in hubs like Loudoun County, Virginia, now average 54 megawatts of power capacity, exceeding the energy draw of major international airports.
The industry faces a structural challenge where reliance on the existing power grid creates direct competition with local communities for energy resources.

posts.title: Learning the Language of the Brain’s Cell Types
posts.summary: How linking neural activity to cell identity will help build models of the brain and reveal new therapeutic targets
bullets: Artificial neural networks rely on uniform computational units, whereas biological brains utilize a diverse array of specialized cell types evolved over millions of years.
The current inability to link specific neuron identities to real-time electrical activity in living brains hinders our understanding of complex cognitive functions and disease pathology.
Researchers propose creating an 'ImageNet for cell types' to standardize a reference dataset that maps specific neuron types to their unique electrical signatures.

Developing this classification system could enable AI to interpret neural recordings from living humans, potentially accelerating the development of biologically realistic AI models and new therapeutic interventions.

posts.title: Overcoming Silicon Photonics Process Control Challenges in the AI Era
posts.summary:
How connected inspection, metrology and software can help manufacturers move SiPh and CPO toward high-volume production.
The post Overcoming Silicon Photonics Process Control Challenges in the AI Era appeared first on Semiconductor Engineering.
bullets: Silicon photonics (SiPh) and co-packaged optics (CPO) are emerging as essential solutions to overcome the power, heat, and latency bottlenecks of traditional copper interconnects.
Optical performance is highly sensitive to small process variations, requiring significantly tighter control over geometry, films, and material defects than standard semiconductor manufacturing.
Manufacturers must implement connected inspection and metrology software to maintain yield as they transition SiPh and CPO technologies from research to high-volume production.

posts.title: Nio opens northernmost swap station in China, touting 3-minute swaps in extreme cold
posts.summary:
Nio has opened its northernmost battery swap station in China in Heihe, Heilongjiang province, where temperatures can fall to -48°C (-54.4°F).
For details, please visit CnEVPost (cnev.co).
bullets: Nio has launched its northernmost battery swap station in Heihe, Heilongjiang, capable of operating in temperatures as low as -48°C.
The station utilizes an insulated, temperature-controlled chamber to maintain battery health between 15°C and 30°C, ensuring 3-minute swap times despite extreme external conditions.
This fifth-generation facility supports Nio's multi-brand strategy, serving Nio, Onvo, and Firefly vehicles.
Nio's national infrastructure now totals 4,262 swap stations, with the company successfully extending its network coverage to the northern, southern, eastern, and western extremities of China.

posts.title: Nio warns owners of 'airbag recall' scam texts as other automakers issue similar alerts
posts.summary:
Scammers impersonate Nio and regulators, using unofficial links to lure owners into submitting personal information.
For details, please visit CnEVPost (cnev.co).
bullets: Nio has issued a formal warning regarding fraudulent text messages impersonating the company to solicit personal data under the guise of an 'airbag recall.'
The scam employs high-pressure tactics, including threats to cancel vehicle warranties, to coerce owners into clicking malicious links and entering credentials on fake login pages.
The incident is part of a broader trend of automotive industry phishing, with brands like Aito, BMW, and Ford reporting similar fraudulent campaigns targeting their customer bases.
